title: Mindfulness: Living in the Moment, Living in the Breath
author: Dhammajiva Thero
edition_analyzed: Standard English Edition (Sati Pasala Foundation translation)
target_audience: People interested in Buddhist meditation practices
Readers who want to reduce stress and anxiety
Those looking to cultivate presence and awareness in daily life
core_themes: Living fully in the present moment
The role of the breath in fostering mindfulness
Understanding the nature of thoughts, feelings, and sensations
The connection between mindfulness practice and inner peace
primary_purpose: To guide readers in cultivating mindfulness by anchoring awareness in the present moment and breath, providing clear meditative instructions, and articulating the transformative benefits of mindful living for greater peace and well-being.

structure_format.organization: Divided into short chapters or dharma talks, each exploring a key aspect of mindfulness and meditation practice

key_concepts_lessons: Mindfulness is cultivated by bringing gentle, sustained attention to the present moment, often through the breath.
Awareness of sensory experiences, thoughts, and emotions is the foundation of mindful living.
Breathing is a universal anchor, accessible to all, which calms the mind and centers attention.
Letting go of judgments and expectations allows for genuine experience and insight.
Mindfulness can be integrated into daily activities—not limited to formal meditation.
Continual practice gradually transforms habitual reactivity into wise response and equanimity.
notable_features: Focus on easily accessible mindfulness practices, suitable for beginners
Draws from classical Buddhist teachings but is secular-friendly
Inclusion of guided practices, exercises, and reflective prompts
cultural_historical_context: Emerging from the contemporary mindfulness movement and rooted in Theravada Buddhist meditation, the book responds to global interest in mindfulness for stress relief, clarity, and well-being, while grounding its teachings in ancient wisdom.
reception_impact: Widely used in mindfulness workshops and retreats, especially in Sri Lanka and South Asia
Popular among both spiritual seekers and secular mindfulness practitioners
Valued for its practical simplicity and gentle encouragement
Not as widely known in Western mainstream circles but respected in Buddhist and meditation communities
comparable_titles: Wherever You Go, There You Are by Jon Kabat-Zinn
The Miracle of Mindfulness by Thich Nhat Hanh
The Heart of the Buddha's Teaching by Thich Nhat Hanh
Mindfulness in Plain English by Bhante Gunaratana
